HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Medium two-shot inside the royal stables of the Moon Palace before dawn. Kim Yushin, unarmoured in a dark coat, stands at the head of a young dapple-grey horse, one hand flat on its neck, offering the lead rope to a fourteen-year-old stable boy who is still crying with his mouth shut, wiping his face on his sleeve. Yushin's face is tired and gentle, almost a smile. Empty stalls recede behind them; one stall door hangs open where the white horse used to stand. A lantern hung on a post at the right rakes across the grey's coat and the boy's wet cheek; straw dust floats in the beam. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = yushin. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Colour #2A5FB8. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
